body: Hello @rodrigorodrigues, it looks like you are building on Java 8 and running against Java 11. There are some known issues around this in Quarkus. There's a dev mail discussion about this here https://groups.google.com/d/msgid/quarkus-dev/CAD%2BL2cxs_%3Di%2B3%2BrcP3-SiO_AcAqBdY_jAVsSzJgQYdmabfJRMQ%40mail.gmail.com
@mkouba maybe we should just ignore @Deprecated, it should not really be used by CDI code anyway, and it is just causing problems.

We've seen similar problems IIRC with some other annotation in the past.
+1 for ignoring it

FWIK we currently ignore `java.lang.constant.ConstantDesc` and `java.lang.constant.Constable` interfaces for the same reason.

We could ignore `@Deprecated` but I'm not a big fan of "exceptions" like this. On the other hand, I can't think of a better solution. So I'll send a PR later today...

For the record - we do create annotation literals for all injection points that resolve to a `@Dependent` bean that injects the `InjectionPoint` metadata. In this particular case, [JWTAuthContextInfoProvider#whitelistAlgorithms](https://github.com/smallrye/smallrye-jwt/blob/master/implementation/src/main/java/io/smallrye/jwt/config/JWTAuthContextInfoProvider.java#L256-L259) resolves to [ConfigProducer#produceOptionalConfigValue](https://github.com/smallrye/smallrye-config/blob/master/implementation/src/main/java/io/smallrye/config/inject/ConfigProducer.java#L110-L115) and we need to simulate `javax.enterprise.inject.spi.InjectionPoint.getAnnotated()`.
